solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Chilled fellow — one like Ice Cube, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: Ice Cube is an American hip-hop artist, so one like him is a rapper

explanation.surface: A cool customer is described as a near-copy of the hip-hop star Ice Cube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ice Cube' pulls toward frozen drinks, which suits the definition but is the misdirection: he is a performer, giving RAPPER, and 'mostly' trims it to RAPPE.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word for iced, used of drinks served over crushed ice, so it means chilled.

clue.text: Dance moves briefly shown by fop?

definitions.text: Dance moves briefly shown by fop?

parts.words: Dance moves briefly shown by fop?
parts.note: read the dandy's word as abbreviations: F for a unit of length and OP, short for opus, a piece of creative labour

explanation.surface: A dandy is said to show off some dance steps in brief.
explanation.walkthrough: This works backwards: abbreviate the two halves of the answer, F for the unit of length and OP (opus) for the creative labour, and you get the clue's 'fop'.
explanation.definitionFit: Skilful placing of the feet in dancing, so the term covers a dancer's moves.

clue.text: Very high and rising somewhat — so miss it, lamentably

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A singer warned that a top note may be missed, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'rising' turns the hidden run upward: OMISSITLA, read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical term for the very highest register, from the Italian superlative of alto.

clue.text: See 12
End of semester, arguably

parts.note: split in three words, the answer says a semester is, arguably, the American word for a school period

explanation.surface: Someone muses on when the academic half-year finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as TERM IN US: a semester is, arguably, what Americans call a school term. The blog instead reads the last letters of semester plus a word for less.
explanation.definitionFit: The last stop of a railway or bus line is its final point, hence an end.

clue.text: Former member of religious order is topless model

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: topless means the first letter goes

parts.note: a Templar was a knight of the medieval military religious order

explanation.surface: An ex-knight from a holy order now poses as a topless model, a tabloid scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like part of the model's description but strips the T from TEMPLAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect example to be copied is a pattern or model.

clue.text: Such a small volume includes Hamlet? On the contrary

definitions.text: Such a small volume includes Hamlet? On the contrary

parts.words: Such a small volume includes Hamlet? On the contrary
parts.note: the reverse holds: the word Hamlet includes the abbreviation ML, the symbol for this tiny volume

explanation.surface: A tiny printed book seems to contain the whole of Shakespeare's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'volume' suggests a book; it is a measure of capacity. ML sits inside haMLet, so the play's name contains the unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousandth part of the metric unit of capacity, a very small volume abbreviated ml.

clue.text: Two things possibly said just before bedtime?

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be arranged another way
two says the word for an object is written out twice

parts.note: a thing is an object; the plural is read as the single word taken more than once

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what people say as they turn in for the evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two things' gives THING THING; 'possibly' rearranges each copy, and both come out the same bedtime word.
explanation.definitionFit: A childlike farewell given when going to bed, the same word repeated.

clue.text: Drunk heading off after "quiet" drink

indicators.note: after puts the trimmed word behind the call for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed

parts.note: merry means tipsy, slightly drunk

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker, head spinning, follows a call for silence with another drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified wine from Jerez in Spain, a classic drink.

clue.text: See 20
Working sailor is given this clue for a lake

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is switched on
tar is an old word for a sailor
this is clue 10, and the digits 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A busy sailor is handed a clue about a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this clue' is clue 10, whose number written as digits resembles the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the five Great Lakes of North America, on the US-Canada border.

clue.text: Poem from Spain (nothing good in this)

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: in says the letters for nothing and good go inside the word for this

parts.note: this refers to the clue itself
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A reader judges a Spanish poem worthless, nothing good in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this' stands for the thing you are reading, a CLUE, and O and G go inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A short pastoral poem, often a dialogue between shepherds, as in Virgil.

clue.text: Rainy after sun's gone in, having left Irish town

indicators.note: gone in says the letter for the sun goes inside the word for rainy

parts.note: wet means rainy
S abbreviates sun, as in weather and calendar shorthand
left is the nautical term for a ship's left-hand side

explanation.surface: A traveller leaves a wet Irish town once the sun has disappeared behind clouds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sun's gone in' reads as weather but puts S inside WET; 'left' is the sailor's word for that side.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in County Mayo in the west of Ireland.

clue.text: Group administered rites for relative after marriage

parts.note: Steps was a British pop group of the late 1990s

indicators.note: rites that are administered are dealt out, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band presides over a ceremony for a family member after a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is the pop group STEPS; 'administered' mixes RITES into ISTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter of one's step-parent, a family tie created by a parent's marriage.

clue.text: Old bike cop lied about in letter

indicators.note: in says the shuffled letters go inside the letter's name

parts.note: vee is the spelt name of the letter V

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman lied in writing about an antique bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letter' wants to be a written note; it is the spelt name of a letter of the alphabet, with 'about' shuffling the policeman's words and 'in' placing them.
explanation.definitionFit: An early form of bicycle, such as the boneshaker or penny-farthing.

clue.text: Bankrupt union, regularly overdrawn?

parts.note: every other letter of union, starting at the first, put inside the colour of debt, since an overdrawn account is in that colour

explanation.surface: A trade union, often in debt, ends up bankrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: Alternate letters of uNiOn give UIN; 'overdrawn' means in the red, so UIN goes in RED. 'Bankrupt' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or company that is bankrupt has been financially wrecked.

clue.text: See 23
Mocking restriction left by Liberal leader

indicators.note: left by means the letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a limitation is a restriction

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Liberal leader leaves behind a mocking restriction.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocking someone by copying their manner is a form of mimicry.

clue.text: Support model that's drunk a lot becoming this?

definitions.text: Support model that's drunk a lot becoming this?

parts.note: a tee supports a golf ball
the Model T was Ford's famous car

indicators.note: drunk means the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Backing a heavy drinker who is giving up alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A LOT into OTAL. The whole clue also describes the outcome: a heavy drinker reformed.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstaining from alcohol completely, the hoped-for state of a reformed drinker.

clue.text: Stone me! Your old deserted sweetheart is under arrest, for a start

indicators.note: is under says, in a down clue, these pieces go below the letter from arrest
for a start means the first letter only

parts.note: thy is the old form of your

indicators.note: deserted means emptied, leaving only the outside letters

explanation.surface: An exclamation of shock: a jilted lover has been arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stone me!' looks like an exclamation, but 'Stone' is the definition. 'deserted' empties SWEETHEART to ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple variety of quartz used as a gemstone.

clue.text: Former US Marine officer shortly to take off 26 from Colne

definitions.text: Former US Marine officer shortly to take off 26 from Colne

parts.words: Former US Marine officer shortly to take off 26 from Colne
parts.note: the town of Colne loses its final E, the east side named by 26, leaving COL N, a rank and a compass point abbreviated

explanation.surface: Instructions for subtracting something from Colne, a Lancashire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Colne is a small town in Lancashire. Take E, its east side (26 is EAST SIDE), and COL N is left: the officer's rank and name shortened.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver North was a lieutenant colonel in the US Marines, known for the Iran-Contra affair.

clue.text: Brief president about Islamic State platitude

indicators.note: about says the shortened name goes round the other letters
brief means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: Donald Trump, US president

explanation.surface: A US president delivers a short, trite remark about Islamic State.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-evident statement so obvious it is not worth saying, a cliche.

clue.text: Book of the month — a third volume

parts.note: Oct is the abbreviation for October

indicators.note: third means the first third of the word, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A book club picks its book of the month, the third volume of a series.
explanation.definitionFit: A book size made by folding sheets into eight leaves, so a book of that format.

clue.text: Musical partner of 9 still

parts.note: 9-down is a compass point, and its opposite pairs with it
still means calm, peaceful

explanation.surface: A musical's partner is still waiting for a cue.
explanation.definitionFit: A Rodgers and Hammerstein stage show of 1949, so a musical.

clue.text: Firmly held belief of prisoner with one leg

parts.note: a convict is a prisoner
I is the Roman numeral for one
on is the cricket term for the leg side of the field

explanation.surface: A one-legged inmate holds fast to his beliefs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side of the field is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongly held opinion or certainty that something is true.

clue.text: See 7
Part of US city partner of 12 left?

parts.note: 12 begins with a compass point, and its opposite pairs with it
the left is one of two flanks, so left is an example of a flank

explanation.surface: A district partners with another on the opposite flank of a city.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of Manhattan in New York City, along the East River.

clue.text: See 26
Increase in use of foreign agents during season's first half

indicators.note: during says the agents go inside the shortened season
first half means only the first three of six letters are kept

parts.note: autumn is a season
G-men are American FBI agents, foreign to a British solver

explanation.surface: More foreign spies are deployed early in the season.
explanation.walkthrough: G-men is US slang for FBI agents, so foreign to the British setter.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something bigger or add to it, as in boosting income.

clue.text: Hear about hot sex in threesome

indicators.note: about says the court word goes round the others

parts.note: to hear a case in court is to try it
in means fashionable, hot
it is slang for sex appeal or sex

explanation.surface: Gossip about a hot three-way romp.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of three, especially the Christian Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

clue.text: In secretive fashion, just tours the 23

indicators.note: tours, as in travels round, says the word for just encloses the other pieces

parts.note: only means just, merely
23 is a compass point, abbreviated as S

explanation.surface: Someone quietly goes round the southern regions.
explanation.walkthrough: '23' is 23-down's compass point, giving S.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something on the quiet, secretly or furtively.

clue.text: After reflection, note what curdles milk

indicators.note: after reflection means the word is mirrored, read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound banknote

explanation.surface: Musing on a note, someone asks what makes milk go sour.
explanation.walkthrough: A tenner is a British ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: An enzyme from calves' stomachs used in cheesemaking to set milk into curds.
